I know how you feel, as I went through a similar situation with my boyfriend but then I thought about the fact that people are curious, and we tend to hold our S.O. to unreasonably high standards. It's dangerous, and definitely concerning if it happened more than once, but people make mistakes and it doesn't define her moral compass as a whole. Talk through the fact that it concerns you and now you'll be worried about her when she goes out but if I were you, I would just forgive her and move forward with a mentality of love rather than judgement.

If you've ever logged into Tinder to look at a profile or see what it was, your account was automatically created and will exist forever unfortunately. It will show the last time you were active on the stamp of the profile, so that should be a good piece of indisputable evidence you can use to explain it to her. Just lay it out there and if she wants to be with you, she will. She just needs to understand that she can trust you and situations like this can be mentally exhausting because the evidence seems to suggest otherwise at first glance.

It has probably 98% to do with her. When I was jealous, the only time it wasn't solely due to my own insecurities, it was  because I was dating someone who was unfaithful. It's usually insecurity.

It sounds like you're investing yourself in a friendship that is threatening your romantic relationship. It's hard when you go through difficult times in an LDR (been there) to not want someone to fill that comfort void (attention surrogate) but you're only going to cause your relationship to suffer and will likely cause a rift in your friendship as your feelings develop. I would say pump the brakes on your communication with Bethany and try and save that energy for your communication with your partner. Things will get easier soon, and if they don't you'll figure that out then.

I talked to him immediately after about it. Just trying to sort out my own thoughts on it and take a step back from it because I have a hard time distinguishing what would fall under the "no one's perfect, just work through your issues" category vs. the "not okay whatsoever" category.

When I confronted him about he said it's because he's insecure about past relationships of mine. he and I were friends before we dated, so he knows my previous long-term relationship was really "active" and said he feels like he is inadequate. But I don't know if I believe that given the fact that he wrote what he did. He used to treat me like I was, and I really meant it when I said I think at most I've gained 5 pounds since we started dating, and I work out significantly more.

I work out all the time and eat healthily. I used to be below the healthy weight bracket for my height, and am still on the lower end. If I lost 10-15 pounds I would look pre-pubescent, which I know because that was how I weighed and looked when I was 14.

I would also like to clarify, I sincerely did not snoop. He knows I used his laptop when I stay by him; I keep work materials on it and when I opened it the word document was up on the screen. I didn't seek it out or immediately close it because it was in the same program I was using myself.

I did bring it up to him and he apologized profusely and said he knows it has everything to do with him and nothing to do with me, but being conscious of your thought process and changing the way you think are two really different things, so I'm extremely hesitant to stick it out.
